question: Which repair and proof boundaries prevent repeated editor defects without duplicate rules, proxy completion or compulsory publication?
trigger: User requested scoped fix/verification skill repair after repeated editor regressions and review against Eric Provencher’s September 11 Astra guidance.
requirements: Prevent proxy completion: exact user action, real consumer and follow-up remain required.
Prefer structural invariant ownership and shared rejecting assertions over caller workarounds or duplicate instructions.
Keep ordinary repairs proportional, preserve corpus/receipt controls, and separate local completion from publication.
Maintain shared source provenance and generated installs without changing protected upstream or other projects.
evidenceReuse: Read prior August 26 unit-first escalation decision and September 6 verifier audit. Preserve anti-duplicate-test intent and truthful product coverage limits; rechecked current rules, validator and actual slash/suggestion proof owners. No historical product pass reused.
summary: Pursue the cut of contradictory and duplicate proof-selection gates. Keep Task lifecycle, focused Patch repair, Verify runtime evidence and Regression corpus semantics; strengthen their existing validator and test owners. Do not introduce another fix skill, proof database, controller or test API.
alternatives: Keep/configure: current exact-reproduction language is sound but contradicted by the unit-only and pushed-ref local gates; wording alone is insufficient.

Delete/merge/inline: remove duplicate Patch runner selection and contradictory unit-only/mandatory-workflow-edit/publication gates; retain distinct proof/corpus jobs instead of merging all skills into a giant itinerary.
Change existing API: repair the existing Regression validation contract for separately justified native proof and evidenced no-change; preserve its schema and receipts.
Add primitive: reject another test wrapper/coverage inventory because canonical selection, focus, event and error helpers already exist.
Move ownership: shared methods remain in Dotai, Plate specifics in source rules, native proof in Verify and product invariants in their package owners.
Replace architecture: a wholesale proof-platform rewrite is unsupported by current evidence; repeated product invariant failures can separately trigger Best API Review before further patches.
proofLimits: Instruction audit and helper semantics only. 85 validator tests and 33 source contracts pass; generated resources and shared provenance are verified. Paired fresh-agent recorded-evidence exercises both pass a blinded six-criterion artifact review; no superiority, speed or actual browser claim. No editor/release sweep. The broad ledger check detects unrelated concurrent browser/ai-session inventory drift; this scoped immutable review records its own source fingerprints.
